chapter: New Orleans pianists and Clarence Williams
title: Sidney Bechet learns saxophone on Clarence Williams's horn
summary: He watched Bechet pick up Williams's saxophone during the Rosebud show and master it within a week.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh yeah, Professor Minetta said he had played up there once.

Yeah, and Bichet, that's the first time I heard Bichet play, Bichet was working for Clarence. And then he had hired a woman to play piano for the show, her name was Emily, Emily Hines I think it was. She played piano for the show and he was the comedian on the show on the stage.

And I used to be up there every day and be at the rehearsals and he had Sweetie Matthews working with him, Octavia Summers, and they had Bichet and that was actually the first saxophone that Bichet ever played was Clarence Williams' saxophone.
Was it an alto or a C melody?

It was a, I'm pretty sure it was a C melody, either alto, but I think it was a C melody. Because anyway, they was on advertisement and Clarence was playing this saxophone and Bichet was playing the clarinet and they had a piano and a wagon and they had the drum. And it was on advertisement and I was on the wagon with them and Bichet was saying he bet he could learn how to play that thing, you know. And so he was fooling around with it and fooling around with it and he blowed a couple of good notes on it and so Clarence told him, he said, well if you think you can learn it, he said, I'm going to let you take it home with you. He said, no. He said, I'm telling you. He said, I don't want you to pawn my home. That's what the Clarence told Bichet. And Bichet said, no, I'm going to bring it, I'm learning. So he come up there that next day and you know he fooled around and he learned how to play a number on it, you know. And so then Clarence Williams let him use the horn and when you find around he could play it better than Clarence, you know. And then Bichet left and went to Chicago and the next time I heard him, he was playing the soprano. He was playing the soprano. He was playing the soprano. So I said, well you know, he was very apt. He learned something right quick. Because he learned how to play that horn so quick and during that time when Clarence had the saxophone, had his saxophone rather, there was a very few saxophones in the city. And if I'm not mistaken, it was between him and Charlie McQuirtus who was the first color that had ever had a saxophone. And there was a very few in the city at all among white-up colored saxophones. And Bichet learned how to play it right now. In a week's time he was playing the double out that C melody. I think it was C melody.
